summary: Round 7 recheck (08:20-08:32 UTC 26 Sep, after the finals read: #37 K2 = 0.954, clean, L (7.36, 7.54] h; #38 twin = 0.953, L (6.69, 6.87] h; finals #37 + #38). It picks three closed ideas that rounds 1-6 did not re-check. Two were measured on CPU on the exp60 x138 lab (56 train clips, final graphs, 7 um per-frame Hungarian, official evaluable-FP rule; same matching as the round-6 stitch replay). None revives and the plan does not change. (A) Tracklet gap-closing g=1..3 and the temporal-sandwich hole fill (I-186, I-141) STAY CLOSED, now by measurement on x138 instead of the v3 desk estimate (~+0.0005 lab). Pairs end(t) -> start(t+g+1) under 20 um: g1 TP 1 / FP 137, g2 TP 2 / FP 149, g3 TP 2 / FP 172. Under 10 um: 2 TP against 63 evaluable FP, plus ~3.9k unevaluable pairs that would each add interpolated nodes. Precision is ~0.03 against a ~0.5 break-even. x138's gap / gap2 stages (8,615 synthetic nodes in the 56 final graphs) already take this class. (B) The z-split of under-segmented nuclei (I-042, with I-128) STAYS CLOSED, and its premise is now measured false on x138. Of 668 missing GT nodes (1,211 FN edge-ends), only 31 (4.6%) are merges, i.e. the nearest final node within 7 um is claimed by another GT node. 30 of them are yx-dominant, 1 is z-dominant, and only 2 GT pairs are <= 4 um apart. 80 (12%) were removed by x138's own tail, and 557 (83%) are absent upstream of the tail. New fact: 71% of the missing nodes (477) have their nearest final node at 7-10 um, and 96% of those nodes are claimed by no GT node (mean |dz| ~4.7 um, |dyx| ~5.6 um). That is a localisation or identity class. Only the detector or head can reach it (post-deadline), not a split, a hole fill or a gap closer. (C) Ideas rejected for runtime and the headroom family (H2 polyphase view I-038, SimView readmit I-144, third detector I-156, deadline moves I-007/I-008, D4 I-009, K2'') STAY CLOSED under the '12 h limit, ~4 h headroom' fact. #37/#38 have already run on the hidden set, which covers public and private in one run, so no runtime idea can change the ticked finals. For any new K2-based file, the binding limit is the 8.0 h in-kernel insertion gate, not 12 h. The slack is >= 0.46 h (8.0 - L(K2)_hi 7.54), less than the 0.58 h GPU run spread. The cheapest headroom rider (H2, +0.38 h at N=106) would also need K2''-style deadlines, a new build, a dummy and an R4 read at >= +0.002 public before R8 (27 Sep 12:00 UTC), in a class that went 0/5 on the LB. Round 1 judged these before the latencies were measured. The measured latencies make the closure final.

findings.what: Tracklet gap-closing LAP g=1..3 (I-186; v3 v_linking-on-x138_tracklet-gap-lap) and hole fill with a temporal sandwich (I-141; v2 hole-fill-sandwich). OLD VERDICT: I-186 was refuted on a desk estimate from exp39 anatomy. The reach was ~173 FN (a_tail ~115 plus <= 58 one-frame bridges), worth ~+0.0005 lab at 0.6 precision. The g=1..3 part was said to overlap gap1/gap2/gapfill, and widening the gap radius 5 -> 6.5 um gave LB -0.001 ('gap closing saturated'). I-141 was refuted on exp39: 73% of hole nodes at 4-6 um sit on the same imaged blob, and a sandwich passes 44% of holes vs 40% of random controls. WHAT CHANGED: both verdicts came from the OLD base. On x138 no one had measured the residual gap class; round 6 measured only g=0. The FN anatomy on x138 is also different: node misses are the largest class (miss 834 of 1,705 FN, round 3). 'Most FN are node misses' could have made hole or gap filling look revivable. MEASURED NOW on exp60 (56 clips, final graphs): pairs of a pred track end at t and a start at t+g+1, labelled against GT. TP needs a GT path a->...->b through g intermediates that no pred node claims, with linear interpolation within 7 um of each GT intermediate. FP needs an evaluable endpoint, following the official rule. Pairs under 20 um: g1 TP 1 / FP 137; g2 TP 2 / FP 149 (+3 GT paths claimed or too far); g3 TP 2 / FP 172 (+5). Under 10 um: g1 1/9, g2 1/25, g3 0/29, i.e. 2 TP vs 63 FP, plus ~3,900 unevaluable pairs that would each add g interpolated nodes. Mutual-NN filtering does not change the picture. Every TP is in 6bba. Among the missing GT nodes, 93 are sandwich holes (both GT neighbours matched), but 81 of those have no presafe node within 4 um and no final node within 7 um. Their neighbours are in continuing pred tracks, so they are not end/start pairs. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED, now by measurement. The ceiling is <= ~5 recoverable gaps in 56 clips (~12 edges, ~+0.0003 at 100% precision), and the real precision is ~0.03 vs a ~0.5 break-even. x138's gap stages already take this class: 5,647 gap_synthetic + 2,968 gap2_synthetic nodes in the 56 final graphs.

findings.what: Valley-gated z-split of under-segmented nuclei (I-042), with the Ultrack-supervised split head (I-128). OLD VERDICT (v3 s_merge, exp39 base): refuted. The net was -0.0003..+0.0003 lab. 97% of same-frame raw-peak pairs under 5 um are z-duplicates. v2 measured that 6bba misses are not a merge problem: close GT pairs under 7 um are 1% of misses. The 44b6 under-segmentation (167 FN) was real but small. WHAT CHANGED: x138 has the V1284 head, readmit and lowrefine (now scored: d1 = d2 = 0), and the node-miss class is the largest FN class on x138 (round 3), so the merge share needed re-measuring on the new base. MEASURED NOW on exp60 (56 clips): 668 GT nodes are missing, i.e. endpoints of FN edges with no match (44b6 64, 6bba 604; 1,211 FN edge-ends). By class: MERGED (the nearest final node within 7 um is claimed by another GT node) 31 = 4.6%, of which yx-dominant 30 and z-dominant 1, with only 2 GT-GT pairs <= 4 um apart. PRUNED BY THE x138 TAIL (presafe node within 4 um, none in final within 7 um) 80 = 12%. ABSENT UPSTREAM 557 = 83%. Nearest final node: < 4 um 2, 4-7 um 29, 7-10 um 477 (71%), 10-15 um 123, >= 15 um 37. Of the 477 at 7-10 um, 456 (96%) are claimed by no GT node. Their offsets are mixed: mean |dz| ~4.7 um, |dyx| ~5.6 um, z-dominant 194 vs yx-dominant 283. NEW VERDICT: STAYS CLOSED, and the premise is now false on x138. The z-merge ceiling is ~1 node in 668, so a z-split can only add duplicates. The dominant residual is a 7-10 um localisation or identity class. Only the detector or coordinate head can reach it, and that is retraining, i.e. post-deadline (R9). The 12% tail-pruned class is the leaf-prune / short-track population already closed on LB anchors (P36, probe 6).

findings.what: x138 node-miss anatomy on the exp60 lab, for the post-deadline agenda. 668 missing GT nodes (1,211 FN edge-ends; 6bba 604 / 44b6 64). Of these, 83% are absent upstream of the tail (no presafe node within 4 um), 12% were removed by x138's tail and 4.6% are merges (only 1 z-dominant). 71% have an unclaimed final node at 7-10 um (mean |dz| ~4.7 um, |dyx| ~5.6 um). The residual FN mass therefore sits in localisation or identity just outside the 7 um match radius, not in missing detections next to a node and not in splits or gaps. All training-free levers measured on x138 are now exhausted: gap/hole (this round), stitch (round 6), swapfix (round 3), leaf prune (round 4), z-split (this round).
